problems.title: Invert a cube-root function
problems.question: Find the inverse of y=∛(0.5x−1).
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: Cube both sides:y³=0.5x−1.
steps: Solving for x gives x=2y³+2. Interchange the variable names.

problems.title: Integers between exponential endpoints
problems.question: Count the integers in[2^(√2−1),3^1.5].
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
steps: The integers are 2,3,4,5.

problems.title: An exponential intercept
problems.question: The graphs9aˣ and a^(x+2) meet on the y-axis. Find the y-intercept of 2a^(x+1).
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: At x=0,9=a². An exponential base is positive, so a=3.
steps: The requested intercept is(0,2a)=(0,6).

problems.title: Angle between rectangle diagonals
problems.question: A cylinder has height 4r. Find the sine of the angle between diagonals of its axial section.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: For rectangle sidesu, v, the sine between diagonals is 2uv/(u²+v²).
steps: Here u=2r, v=4r, so the sine is 16r²/(20r²)=0.8.

problems.title: A spherical section
problems.question: The section diameter plus sphere diameter is 32, and the radii differ by 4. Find plane-centre distance.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: R+r=16, R−r=4, so R=10, r=6. Distance d satisfies d²+r²=R².

problems.title: Reciprocal radical bases
problems.question: Simplify(√2−1)^(2x−1)−(√2+1)^(1−2x).
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
steps: The second power equals(√2−1)^(2x−1), so their difference is 0.

problems.title: Order three logarithms
problems.question: Order a=log₂(√2+1), b=log₃(1/2), c=log_(√3)(√6−2).
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
steps: Since0<√6−2<1/√3, c<−1. Therefore c<b<a.

problems.title: A monotone logarithmic equation
problems.question: How many real roots does x+3+log₂x=0 have?
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: The domain is x>0. Both x and log₂x are strictly increasing.
steps: The expression tends to −∞ at 0+ and to+∞ at∞. Continuity and strict increase give exactly one root, which is positive.

problems.title: A right triangular prism
problems.question: The base has hypotenuse12 and angle 60°; prism height 5. Find volume.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: The legs are 6 and 6√3; V=base are a×height.

problems.title: A tangential right trapezoid prism
problems.question: A right trapezoid has inradius1 and acute angle 30°. Prism height is 5. Find volume.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: Trapezoid altitude=2r=2; slant leg=2/sin30°=4. For a tangential quadrilateral, opposite side sums agree.
steps: The bases sum to 2+4=6. Base are a=(6/2)·2=6, and volume=6·5=30.

problems.title: Simplify a logarithmic product
problems.question: Simplify(logₐb+log_ba+2)(logₐb−log_(ab)b)log_ba.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: Put t=logₐb. Then log_ba=1/t and log_(ab)b=t/(1+t).
steps: The expression becomes[(t+1)²/t]·[t²/(t+1)]·(1/t)=t+1.
problems.note: All original logarithms must be defined; in particular a, b, ab are valid bases where used.

problems.title: A double root in a logarithmic equation
problems.question: If2logₐb+0.5log_ba=2, find b²−a.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: Put t=logₐb≠0. Then2t+1/(2t)=2 gives(2t−1)²=0.
steps: Thus t=1/2, b=√a, and b²−a=0.

problems.title: An exponential equation and a remainder
problems.question: Find the remainder modulo6 of the solution of 3^(2x−15)=9·3^(x−10)+2.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
steps: The roots are 1/9 and −2/27; only 1/9 is positive. Thus x−10=−2, x=8, and the remainder is 2.

problems.title: A square prism inscribed in a sphere
problems.question: A regular square prism has height 4√17 and circumradius10. Find volume.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: The space diagonal is 20, so 2s²+(4√17)²=400.
steps: Hence2s²=128, s²=64. Volume=s²h=256√17.

problems.title: Distance between skew lines in a hexagonal prism
problems.question: A regular hexagonal prism has every edge1. Find the distance between lines F₁D and AC.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
steps: The horizontal projections of the line directions are parallel. Their common perpendicular is horizontal and perpendicular to AC.
With unit normal n=(1/2,√3/2,0), the line separation is|n·(D−A)|=1.

problems.title: Logarithms of reciprocal radicals
problems.question: Simplify log_(√3−1)7·log₇(4−2√3)−log_(√3−√2)(√3+√2).
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
steps: The logarithm product is 2, and the final logarithm is −1. The result is 2−(−1)=3.

problems.title: Express a common logarithm
problems.question: Given log₁₀2=a and log₂7=b, find log₁₀56.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: 56=2³·7; log₁₀7=log₁₀2·log₂7=ab.
steps: Therefore log₁₀56=3a+ab.

problems.title: Angles between longest and shortest prism diagonals
problems.question: A right parallelepiped has base sides 4,5 and height 3. Which listed cosine can occur between a longest and shortest space diagonal?
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: Let base vectors u, v have lengths 4,5 and w⊥base have length 3. The diagonal lengths squared are 50±40cosθ.
steps: For directions u+v+w and u−v+w, the dot product is 16−25+9=0, so cosine 0 occurs.
Using the other height sign gives acute-angle cosine 18/√(2500−1600cos²θ). This equals 0.4 when cos²θ=19/64, which is a valid base angle.
problems.answer: Both 0 and 0.4 are possible listed answers.
problems.note: The choice of the two space diagonals is not unique. The question has at least these two valid listed answers;0.6 would require a degenerate base and 1 is impossible.

problems.title: Section through a tetrahedron’s height midpoint
problems.question: A regular tetrahedron has edge4. A section contains a base edge and the height midpoint. Find its are a.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: In the perpendicular symmetry plane, let M be that edge midpoint, C the opposite base vertex, O the base centre, S the apex. MC=2√3, MO=2√3/3, SO=4√(2/3).
steps: The line from M through the midpoint of SO meets SC one quarter of the way from S to C. Its intersection T has horizontal coordinate√3 and height 3SO/4.
Thus MT²=3+(9/16)(32/3)=9. Section are a=AB·MT/2=4·3/2=6.

problems.title: Distance to a cone section plane
problems.question: A cone has radius 6, height 4. A plane through its apex cuts a 120° base arc. Find its distance from the base centre.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: The chord is at distance 6cos60°=3 from the centre. In a perpendicular cross-section, the plane trace joins(3,0) to(0,4).
steps: Its equation is 4x+3z−12=0. Distance from(0,0) is 12/√(4²+3²)=12/5.

problems.title: A sixth-root exponential substitution
problems.question: Find the digit sum of the solution of 4·9^(⁶√x)−9·4^(⁶√x)=5·6^(⁶√x).
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: Put t=⁶√x≥0, z=(3/2)^t. Dividing by 6^t gives 4z−9/z=5.
steps: Then4z²−5z−9=0, with positive root 9/4=(3/2)². Thus t=2, x=64, and digit sum 10.

problems.title: Powers of logarithms
problems.question: Find the sum of real roots of[log₁₀((x−1)²)]⁴+[log₁₀((x−1)³)]²=25.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: The cubic logarithm requires x>1. Put t=log₁₀(x−1), giving16t⁴+9t²−25=0.
steps: Thus x=11 or 1.1, and their sum is 12.1.

problems.title: An exponential-logarithmic system
problems.question: If8(√2)^(x+3)=0.5^(y−3) and log₃(x−2y)+log₃(3x+2y)=3, find xy.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: Comparing powers of 2 gives x+2y=−3. Log addition gives(x−2y)(3x+2y)=27.
steps: Substitute2y=−3−x:the product is(2x+3)(2x−3)=27, so x=±3.
Only x=3 gives positive log arguments9 and 3; then y=−3.

problems.title: A cube section plane angle
problems.question: In a cube, M is midpoint of AD and N of DD₁. Find the cosine between planes MNC and A₁B₁C₁D₁.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
steps: A normal to MNC is(−1,2,−2). The top plane has normal(0,0,1). The acute normal cosine is 2/3.

problems.title: Lateral faces of an oblique triangular prism
problems.question: An oblique prism has equilateral base side 4, lateral edges√13 making60° with the base, and one rectangular lateral face. Find the sum of the other two face areas.
problems.idea: Use inverse operations, a substitution, or a perpendicular geometric section.
formulas: The lateral edge’s horizontal projection has length √13/2 and is perpendicular to the rectangular face’s base side.
steps: Its projection onto each other base-side direction has magnitude√39/4. Each remaining parallelogram are a is 4√[13−(√39/4)²]=13.
The two areas sum to 26.
